subtitle: The SNMP objects for monitoring and configuring the radio links of DOCSIS cable modems and their head-end systems.

tldr.problem: Cable operators needed a standard way to manage the radio frequency interfaces of DOCSIS cable modems and cable modem termination systems with SNMP.
tldr.mechanism: The MIB module defines tables of managed objects in three groups: ones for both modems and head-end systems, ones for modems only, and ones for head-end systems only. It also explains how these interfaces map onto the standard Interfaces MIB.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2670 was a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 4546.

today: RFC 2670 was a Proposed Standard published in August 1999 and has been obsoleted by RFC 4546, which replaces it.

sections.title: What This MIB Covers
sections.content:
RFC 2670 defines a MIB (Management Information Base) module for SNMP-based management of MCNS/DOCSIS compliant Radio Frequency (RF) interfaces. It is written in SMIv2 and was produced by the IPCDN working group. The objects are derived in part from the DOCSIS Radio Frequency Interface Specification.

The glossary explains the vocabulary. A CM (cable modem) is the slave station in a DOCSIS system. A CMTS (cable modem termination system) is the master station in the head-end: it is the only station that transmits downstream and it schedules upstream transmissions by its cable modems. Downstream runs from head-end to subscriber, upstream the other way.
sections.eli5: A cable modem is the box in your home, and the head-end box is the boss at the cable company. This document gives names to the gauges on both ends of the cable.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB
sections.content:
The MIB has three groups. docsIfBaseObjects applies to both modems and head-end systems and has tables for downstream channels, upstream channels, Quality of Service profiles and signal quality. docsIfCmObjects is for cable modems only, with a MAC table and a service table for upstream queues. docsIfCmtsObjects is for head-end systems only, with tables such as status, per-modem status, service queues, modulation profiles and a MAC-to-modem lookup.

Rows created automatically by the device generally mix configuration and status objects. Rows meant to be created by a management station are generally restricted to configuration (read-create) objects.
sections.eli5: Some gauges are on both boxes, some only on the home box, and some only on the cable company's box.

sections.title: Relationship to the Interfaces MIB
sections.content:
An ifEntry exists for each RF downstream interface, each RF upstream interface and each RF MAC layer, and the ifStackTable MUST be implemented to show how they relate. The RF MAC interface sits on top of the downstream and upstream interfaces. The interface types are docsCableMaclayer(127), docsCableDownstream(128) and docsCableUpstream(129).

A downstream interface is output-only at the CMTS, so its input counters return zero, and input-only at the modem, so its output counters return zero. The ifTestTable and ifRcvAddressTable are not supported, and the medium does not support virtual circuits. The same model can describe Telco Return systems, where upstream traffic uses other MIBs such as PPP or Modem MIBs.
sections.eli5: The main connection sits on top of one pipe coming down and one or more pipes going up, and each gets its own meter.

sections.title: Conformance and Security
sections.content:
The compliance statement docsIfBasicCompliance makes the base group mandatory. The cable modem group is implemented only in modems, and the head-end group only in cable modem termination systems.

The security section warns that improper manipulation of these objects may deny service to a large number of end users. Changing the QoS profile objects may let a user improve their own service or reduce other subscribers' service. The MIB does not affect confidentiality, authentication or authorization. For authentication and authorization it points to the related cable device MIB, and for confidentiality the working group expected to issue a MIB for DOCSIS Baseline Privacy.
